extraction.name: Common Corpus
extraction.description: Common Corpus is the largest open dataset for LLM pre-training, containing approximately 2 trillion tokens of data that are either uncopyrighted or under permissible licenses. It is multilingual, covering a wide variety of languages from main European languages to low-resource ones, and includes code data. It is organized into six collections: Open Government, Open Culture, Open Science, Open Web, Open Code, and Open Semantic.
extraction.license: Public Domain, CC-By, MIT, CC-By-SA, Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, and other open licenses
extraction.creator: PleIAs
extraction.inLanguage: en, fr, de, es, la, it, pl, el, pt, ru, and many others
extraction.citeAs: Langlais, P.-C., Rosas Hinostroza, C., Nee, M., Amett, C., Chizhov, P., Jones, E. K., Girard, I., Mach, D., Stasenko, A., & Yamshchikov, I. P. (2025). Common Corpus: The Largest Collection of Ethical Data for LLM Pre-Training. arXiv:2506.01732.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from a wide variety of sources including cultural heritage institutions, government and legal databases, scientific repositories, code repositories, web sources (Wikipedia, Wikisource, YouTube, StackExchange), and semantic data (Wikidata). Collection methods included APIs, bulk downloads, Collections As Data (CAD) initiatives, and direct retrieval from open data portals.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web API, Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Web Scraping, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include: SEC annual reports, WTO documents, AMF documents, EU Tenders (TED), GATT Library, Europarl, Caselaw Access Project, CourtListener, EUR-lex, Eurovoc, French Open Data, USPTO, UN Digital Library, OECD, digitized books and newspapers from national libraries (Library of Congress, French National Library/Gallica, Europeana, German Digital Library, etc.), OpenAlex scientific papers, arXiv, The Stack v1 and v2 (code), Wikipedia, Wikisource, YouTube Commons, StackExchange, and Wikidata.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Documents span from 1618 (Europeana Newspapers) to 2024 (SEC, WTO). Dataset collection began in May 2023 and the current version was released in February 2025.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Wikidata items and properties were translated into formal natural language sequences: 'Q41309 | P:27 | Q171150' becoming 'Franz Liszt country of citizenship Kingdom of Hungary'. PII was replaced with fictitious but realistic values rather than removed or tagged.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Preprocessing included: (1) text segmentation using Segmentext; (2) OCR error detection using OCRoscope and OCRerrcr; (3) OCR correction using OCRonos (based on Llama 3 8B); (4) PII removal using Microsoft Presidio; (5) toxicity detection and filtering using Celadon classifier; (6) for code data: removal of unwanted file types and formats, license filtering, manual quality filters, removal of files with 75%+ digits, and normalization of line endings.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Toxicity annotation: a multilingual toxicity classifier (Celadon) was trained on 2M annotated samples to identify toxic and harmful content along five dimensions: race and origin-based bias, gender and sexuality-based bias, religious bias, ability bias, and violence and abuse. Rights verification for Open Culture followed specific criteria including author life and data object creation time.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Microsoft Presidio (PII detection and replacement), Celadon (DeBERTa-v3-small toxicity classifier), OCRoscope (OCR quality detection based on cld2), OCRerrcr (DeBERTa-v2-style OCR error detection), OCRonos (Llama 3 8B-based OCR correction), Segmentext (text segmentation), fastText (language identification)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Common Corpus will remain an evolving resource. HuggingFace will ensure proper archiving of past versions for reproducibility. Future plans include collecting more data in European languages as part of the LLMs4EU project and expanding coverage for African languages.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) including phone numbers, email addresses, and IP addresses was identified and replaced. PII removal was applied using Microsoft Presidio.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Common Corpus aims to support open LLM research and development while meeting legal and regulatory requirements, including EU AI regulations. It contributes to the AI Commons and open science infrastructure. It enables development of multilingual models supporting low-resource languages and helps avoid legal challenges related to copyright infringement.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Historical texts in Open Culture may contain outdated cultural norms and harmful language regarding ethnic groups, women, and violence. Web data may contain sexual content, hate speech, and racial and gender biases. Low-resource languages are underrepresented. Open Science collection has limited linguistic diversity with ~85% of documents in English.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Common Corpus does not cover the full range of available open data (open data paradox). Coverage for low-resource languages is shallow. The 2 trillion tokens is suitable for pre-training models of limited size but larger models require more data. The dataset does not contain instruction-tuning data and is not directly suitable for task-specific fine-tuning. Curation methods cannot guarantee 100% accuracy in toxicity detection or PII removal.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Primary use case is LLM pre-training. Can be used alone or combined with other open datasets. Also used for: multimodal dataset creation, classifier training, synthetic dataset generation, benchmark creation, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) models, speech foundation models, and historical language model development. Not suitable for instruction-tuning or task-specific fine-tuning directly.

name.evidence: In this paper, we introduce Common Corpus, the largest open dataset for language model pre-training.

description.evidence: The data assembled in Common Corpus are either uncopyrighted or under permissible licenses and amount to about two trillion tokens. The dataset contains a wide variety of languages, ranging from the main European languages to low-resource ones rarely present in pre-training datasets; in addition, it includes a large portion of code data.

license.evidence: The majority of the data in Common Corpus is in the public domain (see Table 3). The license for each document is provided in the metadata, so the dataset can be easily filtered by license as needed for a particular use case.

datePublished.evidence: The current version of Common Corpus, the one we describe in this paper, was released in February 2025 for the Paris AI Summit.

inLanguage.evidence: Common Corpus is multilingual (see Figure 1 and Table 2 for language coverage). Unlike many pretraining mixes, which are composed mostly of English and code data, our dataset has strong representation for several languages, with the top nine languages constitute at least 10B tokens each.

isLiveDataset.evidence: Common Corpus will remain an evolving resource reflecting the need for a continuous open infrastructure rather than a fixed dataset, with HuggingFace ensuring a proper archiving of past versions for reproducibility.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: A large part of Open Culture is compiled from Collections As Data (CAD) — large dumps of texts, datasets, PDFs, and even raw XML output (METS/ALTO). All other parts of Open Culture have been collected on a resource-by-resource basis using APIs and other standard retrieval methods whenever available.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: All other parts of Open Culture have been collected on a resource-by-resource basis using APIs and other standard retrieval methods whenever available. The largest extractions of this kind include Internet Archive (about 2 million monographs in multiple languages) and Delpher (50,000 Dutch monographs and periodicals filtered to match the Dutch copyright law for public domain).

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: Open Government is a set of financial, legal, and administrative data in the public domain... The Open Science collection was made possible largely due to the recent development of OpenAlex... The code data we use comes from the Stack v1 and v2... Open Web collection currently includes four major web sources: Wikipedia and Wikisource... YouTube Commons... StackExchange.

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: Common Corpus was first conceptualized in May 2023 as a French corpus for the French public services... The current version of Common Corpus, the one we describe in this paper, was released in February 2025 for the Paris AI Summit.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: Data processing involved the translation of items and properties into formal language sequences as simple natural language sequences, without textual synthesis: 'Q41309 | P:27 | Q171150' becoming 'Franz Liszt country of citizenship Kingdom of Hungary'... Instead, we replace PII with fictuous but realistic values.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: To prepare the collection, we ran a pipeline of varied filters. We first removed files that were not in our desired set of languages and formats... We then filtered out the licenses to keep only permissible ones. To discard the low-quality data, we ran a series of manual filters... To identify and replace PII, we use Microsoft's Presidio... We developed a pipeline to filter the public domain training data.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: We created a multilingual toxicity classifier, Celadon, a DeBERTa-v3-small model (~140M parameters), which we trained from scratch on 2M annotated samples. Celadon identifies toxic and harmful content along five dimensions: race and origin-based bias, gender and sexuality-based bias, religious bias, ability bias, and violence and abuse.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: To identify and replace PII, we use Microsoft's Presidio... We created a multilingual toxicity classifier, Celadon, a DeBERTa-v3-small model (~140M parameters)... OCRoscope. This is a tool based on the language identification tool cld2... OCRerrcr. This is a DeBERTa-v2-style language model with 400M parameters... We developed OCRonos model based on Llama 3 8B... Language distribution was computed using the fastText language identification model.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: Common Corpus will remain an evolving resource reflecting the need for a continuous open infrastructure rather than a fixed dataset, with HuggingFace ensuring a proper archiving of past versions for reproducibility.

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: Personally Identifiable Information (PII), which is any information that can be used to distinguish or trace an individual's identity, is protected under legislation such as GDPR... In an analysis of large open datasets, there is a staggering amount of personal data in widely used datasets, e.g., large quantities of phone numbers in RedPajama, email addresses in S2ORC and peS2o, and IP addresses in the Stack.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Common Corpus aims to support the pre-training of fully open and auditable LLMs by making it legal to release the source even without the provision of fair use... Through the release of this dataset, we show that open LLM research and development is possible while meeting legal and regulatory requirements—even in the EU, where AI regulations are currently the strictest.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Many texts there are historical periodicals and monographs from at least 80 years ago. Cultural norms surrounding the discussion of certain ethnic groups, women, and themes such as violence have changed dramatically. Many of these texts, therefore, do not meet modern ethical standards... Due to the specificity of open scientific publishing, the Open Science collection has less linguistic diversity, with nearly 85% of documents currently available in English.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Common Corpus is far from collecting the whole range of available open data, which we call the open data paradox... even though the language diversity of the data is large, the coverage for low-resource languages is still shallow... Common Corpus naturally does not contain data for instruction-tuning and any forms of specialized tasks. Therefore, it is not directly suitable for task-specific fine-tuning... none of the curation methods could naturally facilitate a hundred-percent accuracy.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: Common Corpus can be used on its own or in conjunction with existing open datasets, according to one's needs and the desired use case of a language model... It has been used to create a wider range of language model artifacts, including multimodal datasets, classifiers, synthetic datasets, and benchmarks... Common Corpus naturally does not contain data for instruction-tuning and any forms of specialized tasks. Therefore, it is not directly suitable for task-specific fine-tuning.
